title: One Atom, Many Lives: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
subject: Chemistry
objective: In 1847 James Simpson found that chloroform, CHCl₃, could put people to sleep for surgery. Replace a hydrogen of a hydrocarbon with a halogen and you get a haloalkane (halogen on an sp³ alkyl carbon) or a haloarene (halogen on an sp² ring carbon). They are everywhere: chloramphenicol for typhoid, thyroxine with four iodine atoms, chloroquine for malaria, halothane for anaesthesia. The polar C–X bond, with a δ+ carbon, is why they react, and it opens the whole chapter.

fill.q: Replacing an H of a hydrocarbon by a halogen gives a ____ compound.
In a haloalkane the halogen is attached to an ____ hybridised carbon.
In a haloarene the halogen is attached to an ____ hybridised carbon.

tf.q: Chloramphenicol is a chlorine-containing antibiotic used against typhoid.
In the C–X bond, the halogen carries a partial positive charge.
tf.explain: X is more electronegative: X is δ−, C is δ+.
All its carbons are sp³: a haloalkane.

tf.q: C–I is the weakest carbon–halogen bond.
tf.explain: It is the longest C–X bond.

ar.a: Assertion: The carbon of a C–X bond is attacked by nucleophiles. Reason: Carbon carries a partial positive charge.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.

ar.a: Assertion: Benzyl chloride is a haloarene. Reason: It contains a benzene ring.
ar.r: Assertion false (Cl is on an sp³ CH₂ carbon: a haloalkane); reason true.

mcq.explain: They release Cl radicals in the stratosphere.

num.q: Count the halogen atoms in halothane, CF₃CHClBr.
How many hydrogens of methane are replaced in chloroform?

short.q: Define haloalkanes and haloarenes with an example each.
short.solution: Haloalkane: X on an sp³ alkyl carbon, e.g. C₂H₅Cl. Haloarene: X on an sp² ring carbon, e.g. C₆H₅Cl.

short.q: Why is the C–X bond polar?
short.solution: X is more electronegative than C; electrons shift to X, making C δ+ and X δ−.

short.q: Name four useful halogen compounds and their uses.
Who discovered chloroform's anaesthetic use, and when?
Give two environmental problems caused by halogen compounds.
short.solution: Freons deplete ozone; DDT builds up in food chains.
